pages.text: Cooking time is the recipe time divided by $(item)half the size$(), never by less than 1. One coal takes 1200 ticks, one log 600 ticks.

$(l)Time per coal / per log$()$(li)$(item)1x1$() and $(item)2x2$(): 60 s / 30 s$(li)$(item)3x3$(): 40 s / 20 s$(li)$(item)4x4$(): 30 s / 15 s$(li)$(item)5x5$(): 24 s / 12 s$(li)$(item)6x6$(): 20 s / 10 s$(br2)A 2x2 is no faster than a single block, so jump straight to $(item)3x3$() or more.

The oven still cooks $(item)one item at a time$(): a bigger oven gives the same coke per coal, only sooner. The by-products are made $(item)every tick$() the oven cooks, whatever its size, so a fast oven makes the same flow of fluid per second as a slow one, just less of it per coal.
Watch the progress with Engineer's Goggles: it counts down the seconds left on the current item.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
